grounding.states: A dark, quiet room can help babies sleep
grounding.from: Mayo Clinic: A dark, quiet room can help babies sleep.

grounding.states: Naps work best at the same time each day and for about the same length of time
grounding.from: Mayo Clinic: Babies get the most out of naps if they take them at the same time each day and for about the same length of time.

grounding.states: Put him down drowsy but awake so he learns to fall asleep on his own
grounding.from: Mayo Clinic: put babies to bed drowsy but awake, since they sleep best when drowsy. Boys Town Hospital: Teach the child to fall asleep on their own

grounding.states: A calm routine, such as a story read in a calming voice, helps
grounding.from: Ireland's HSE: A consistent daily routine helps... a story read in a calming voice.

grounding.states: Nap in his own bed or crib
grounding.from: Boys Town Hospital: a toddler at home should nap in his own bed or crib.

grounding.states: For babies, sleep on their back with no blankets, stuffed toys or soft items in the crib
grounding.from: Safety (Mayo Clinic, for babies): Put babies to sleep on their backs, with no blankets, stuffed toys or other soft items in the crib or bassinet.

value.answer: It depends a lot on his age, but these work for babies and toddlers: nap at the same time each day and for about the same length of time, keep the room dark and quiet, and use a calm routine like a story or a lullaby. Try putting him down drowsy but still awake so he learns to fall asleep on his own, and have him nap in his own bed or crib. If he's a baby, always put him down on his back with nothing soft in the crib. How old is he?
